findings.impact: A new combat-specific API should not silently break or inherit this noncombat reuse. If this path is production-reachable, it needs its own rules-core constrained amount-distribution validator/API.
findings.pattern: divideOnResolution reuses PlayerController.assignCombatDamage for noncombat amount division and directly writes returned amounts to a damage map.

findings.impact: Current CR makes Damage Assignment Order obsolete. If Forge retains the legacy rules option, the core must expose/validate any required permutation as a legal decision rather than trusting a controller-provided ordering.
findings.pattern: legacy orderBlockers/orderAttackers callbacks are controller-owned when GameRules.orderCombatants is enabled.

findings.impact: Positive architectural precedent: Forge already centralizes validation for neighboring combat decisions, supporting a bounded remediation rather than a new external rules engine.
findings.pattern: Attacker and blocker declarations use CombatUtil.validateAttackers / validateBlocks.

not_claimed: No FORGE_RULES_DEFECT is claimed; source topology/validation ownership is defective, not proven MTG runtime semantics at a correctly constructed state.
scope_note: Only controller-boundary findings directly adjacent to the AF04 pattern were inspected; this is not a full Forge decision-surface audit.
